requirements.requirement: Make the currently supplied DNS nameserver persistent on node1.
requirements.summary: The initial resolver contained the sole supplied nameserver 10.100.120.1. It was added to the eth0 dhcpcd policy, verified while healthy before restart, and directly observed in both the persistent policy and live resolver after a confirmed reboot.

requirements.requirement: Add infra.test as the system search domain on node1.
requirements.summary: The installed dhcpcd policy specifies domain_search=infra.test. The live resolver showed search infra.test after reload and again following the confirmed reboot, demonstrating persistent system-level application.

overall_summary: Both requested DNS outcomes are satisfied with direct pre-restart, disruption, and post-restart evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol for the sole managed node is coherent and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities. Operational hygiene was strong aside from two retained temporary files.
limitations: The generic lifecycle failed-service observation was unsupported because it probes systemd on an Alpine/OpenRC node; relevant OpenRC services were nevertheless checked directly before and after restart.

Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory /etc/dhcpcd.conf, so persistence verification relies on the executor's direct post-restart command output, which is internally coherent and boot-identity corroborated.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive system mutations—candidate validation, persistent dhcpcd configuration, reload, and restart—had clear task or verification roles. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, connection disruption, changed boot identity, and recovered resolver, DNS behavior, networking, SSH, chronyd, and management service state. The only unnecessary retained mutations were two low-risk temporary artifacts: /tmp/dhcpcd-dns-test.conf from candidate testing and /tmp/infraset-node-reboot.log from restart initiation. Both remained after execution and were not cleaned. No new listener exposure or package-health regression was observed.
